```{r setup}
library(yourhonor)
```

Evidence is descriptive until a policy says what it must show. This article
gathers the three kinds of evidence about the synthetic judge from
`vignette("yourhonor")` (calibration, bias probes and stability), assesses
them under one explicit policy, and writes the assessment as a portable
artifact.

## Gather the evidence

The judge and the three calls are the ones `vignette("yourhonor")`,
`vignette("bias-probes")` and `vignette("stability")` explain. Every call
carries the same `audit_id`, which is what lets `report()` bind them.

```{r}
keyword_judge <- function(data) {
  hedged <- grepl("probably|somewhere|should be|I think|I believe|might|sometimes|could", data$input)
  concrete <- grepl("Answer: (Open|Use|Yes)|click", data$input)
  label <- ifelse(hedged, "P", ifelse(concrete, "C", "I"))
  # The flaw under audit: a long input reads as one level more complete.
  long <- nchar(data$input) > 240
  label[long & label == "P"] <- "C"
  label[long & label == "I"] <- "P"
  # A little run-to-run error, so repeated runs are not identical.
  noise <- runif(nrow(data)) < 0.05
  label[noise] <- sample(c("I", "P", "C"), sum(noise), replace = TRUE)
  tibble::tibble(.item_id = data$.item_id, label = label)
}

cal <- calibrate_judge(
  synthetic_gold,
  judge = keyword_judge,
  human_cols = c("rater_1", "rater_2", "rater_3"),
  input_cols = c("input", "target"),
  id_col = "id",
  label_levels = c("I", "P", "C"),
  scale = "ordinal",
  n_boot = 500,
  seed = 1,
  provenance = list(model = "synthetic keyword judge", prompt_version = "v1"),
  audit_id = "synthetic-judge-v1"
)
bias <- probe_bias(
  synthetic_gold,
  keyword_judge,
  input_cols = c("input", "target"),
  probes = c("verbosity", "self_preference", "bandwagon"),
  seed = 1,
  audit_id = "synthetic-judge-v1"
)
stability <- test_retest(
  synthetic_gold,
  keyword_judge,
  input_cols = c("input", "target"),
  n_runs = 5,
  label_levels = c("I", "P", "C"),
  weights = "ordinal",
  n_boot = 500,
  seed = 1,
  audit_id = "synthetic-judge-v1"
)
```

## Declare the policy

`report()` is descriptive unless it receives an acceptance policy. Policy checks
use confidence bounds and distinguish failure, missing evidence, and statistical
indeterminacy. Thresholds that only apply inside a gate (`max_pairwise_disagreement`
for stability, `required_probes` for bias) must be supplied with that gate and
are rejected without it, so a policy never carries a threshold the assessment
does not read. Declare thresholds from the task's error costs, not from a
package-wide notion of a "good" score.

```{r}
policy <- acceptance_policy(
  min_agreement_lower = 0.75,
  min_n = 150,
  min_class_n = 20,
  min_recall = c(I = 0.80, P = 0.75, C = 0.85),
  min_precision = c(C = 0.85),
  max_missing_rate = 0.01,
  max_pairwise_disagreement = 0.10,
  min_stability_n = 150,
  min_stability_runs = 3,
  max_stability_missing_rate = 0.01,
  required_probes = c("verbosity", "self_preference", "bandwagon"),
  min_probe_n = 150,
  max_probe_flip_rate = 0.10,
  max_probe_directional_rate = 0.10,
  max_probe_missing_rate = 0.01,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  coefficient = "gwet_ac2"
)
verdict <- report(cal, bias = bias, stability = stability, policy = policy)
verdict
```

## Read the decision

`report()` returns a `yourhonor_report` whichever `output` you choose; `output`
only sets the default rendering. `verdict$decision` is the overall outcome,
`verdict$checks` holds one row per check with the observed `value`, the
comparison `op`, and the numeric `threshold`, and
`format(verdict, output = "md")` gives the Markdown lines.

```{r}
verdict$decision
verdict$checks[verdict$checks$status != "PASS", c("check", "status", "value", "op", "threshold")]
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
checks <- verdict$checks
# "\x60" is a backtick: inline code cannot contain one literally.
code <- function(x) paste0("\x60", x, "\x60")
n_status <- function(status) sum(checks$status == status)
# One phrase per check, read from the table: "`recall_I`, whose lower bound
# of 0.772 must be >= 0.8".
describe_checks <- function(status) {
  rows <- checks[checks$status == status, ]
  if (nrow(rows) == 0L) return("none")
  side <- sub(" .*$", "", rows$op)
  comparison <- sub("^\\S+ ", "", rows$op)
  phrases <- sprintf(
    "`%s`, whose %s bound of %.3f must be %s %s",
    rows$check, side, rows$value, comparison, format(rows$threshold)
  )
  paste(phrases, collapse = "; ")
}
n_incorrect <- sum(cal$items$human_consensus == "I", na.rm = TRUE)
```

The outcome may be `PASS`, `FAIL`, `NOT_ASSESSED`, or `INDETERMINATE`. That is
intentional: absence of a probe and an underpowered probe are different facts.
Of the `r nrow(checks)` checks here, `r n_status("PASS")` pass,
`r n_status("FAIL")` fail and `r n_status("INDETERMINATE")` are
`INDETERMINATE`, so the decision is `r code(verdict$decision)`.

The failures are the planted flaw: `r describe_checks("FAIL")`. The verbosity
probe pads answers past the judge's 240-character threshold, and the labels
move towards the longer version far more often than the ceiling allows.

The `INDETERMINATE` checks are `r describe_checks("INDETERMINATE")`. Their
intervals overlap the threshold, so the evidence neither clears nor fails
it. Recall on `I`, for instance, rests on the `r n_incorrect` items whose
human consensus is incorrect; a probe that reports `no_signal` can still have
an interval that does not exclude the ceiling. None of these is a `PASS`, and
none is reported as one. Required evidence that was never supplied is
`NOT_ASSESSED`, never silently passed:

```{r}
unprobed <- report(cal, stability = stability, policy = policy)
unprobed$decision
unprobed$checks[unprobed$checks$status == "NOT_ASSESSED", c("check", "status")]
```

## Write an artifact

`write_audit()` writes the same assessment as a Markdown report or as a
versioned JSON summary (`yourhonor.audit.v1`). An existing file is never
replaced unless `overwrite = TRUE`, so a re-run cannot clobber an earlier audit.

```{r}
path <- tempfile("judge-audit-", fileext = ".json")
write_audit(cal, path, bias = bias, stability = stability, policy = policy)
```

```{r, eval = requireNamespace("jsonlite", quietly = TRUE)}
audit <- jsonlite::read_json(path)
audit$decision
names(audit)
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
unlink(path)
```

The JSON artifact contains aggregate calibration evidence, policy checks, and
provenance at full numeric precision, with `null` for every absent value.
Full precision is the stored doubles', not the estimates': irrCAC rounds each
agreement coefficient to five decimals, and its bootstrap bounds inherit that.
Calibration item rows are omitted, but caller-supplied provenance is written
verbatim; keep secrets and raw item content out of provenance fields.
`?write_audit` documents the schema.

## Statistical scope

The item bootstrap and exact class intervals assume independent sampling units.
Do not count repeated templates, users, conversations, or epochs as independent
items. Use a frozen, representative, held-out calibration set that was not used
to tune the judge or prompt, and record the data split/version/hash plus the
model and prompt versions in `provenance`. Confidence levels describe each
interval, not a simultaneous band over every estimate. This synthetic example
demonstrates APIs; it is not deployment evidence.
